items.title: King's brother Andrew arrested
items.description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has reportedly been arrested at his eastern England home. Follow live.

items.title: The names of the 11 'ISIS brides' trying to leave Syria to come to Australia
items.description: The ABC can reveal the names of the 11 women connected to former Islamic State fighters in Syria who attempted to journey home to Australia this week.

items.title: No longer an elitist fantasy, EVs are becoming more affordable
items.description: The price tag of EVs has been a barrier to uptake. As cheaper models hit the market, will more drivers go electric?

items.title: Voters divided as Joyce backflips on vow not to recontest seat
items.description: One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce says he might recontest his seat of New England as a candidate for One Nation if the party needs him to.

items.title: Will this helmet prevent concussions in footballers?
items.description: A lot of research has gone in to treating concussions, but now scientists are testing a new helmet to see if it can prevent them before they happen.

items.title: Live: Skiers rattled after Canadian's scary halfpipe crash
items.description: Canadian Cassie Sharpe goes down hard in the second run of the Winter Olympics freeski halfpipe qualifying, featuring Australian 16-year-old Indra Brown. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Wilson walks back suggestion Liberals would rethink RBA mandate
items.description: Shadow Treasurer Tim Wilson has walked back his call to overhaul the Reserve Bank of Australia's twin focus on taming inflation and full employment. Follow live.

items.title: Taylor walks a tightrope on immigration policy as Hanson surges
items.description: The rifts in Australia's social cohesion can be seen in the blow-up over the so-called ISIS brides and their children, who want to come to Australia.

items.title: Grace Tame event to proceed despite pressure for cancellation
items.description: An International Women's Day event in Bendigo featuring former Australian of the Year Grace Tame will go ahead despite calls for it to be cancelled.

items.title: Amy Taylor's Vogue shoot goes from champagne and ice cream to legal fight
items.description: What began as a photo shoot with champagne, ice cream and humorous glamour shots of Amy Taylor, singer from punk band Amyl and the Sniffers, has escalated into a legal fight over copyright, the US Constitution and an application for a restraining order.

items.title: People poking penguins with sticks, handling 'by the neck'
items.description: Each summer, tourists flock to Tasmanian beaches to marvel at penguins, but for some, admiring the birds from afar is not enough.

items.title: Live: ASX set to open lower, as Wall Street slumps
items.description: The ASX 200 is set to open lower in morning trade, following a slump on Wall Street. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Police descend on semi-rural home in hunt for kidnapped Sydney grandfather
items.description: Police believe they have found a "stronghold" used by the kidnappers of Chris Baghsarian in Dural as the search for the 85-year-old continues.

items.title: Trump suggests decision on Iran likely within 10 days
items.description: Speaking at the inaugural "Board of Peace" meeting in Washington DC, the US president warns "bad things" will happen if a "meaningful deal" isn't reached in nuclear talks with Iran.

items.title: 'Clearly artworks': Arts lawyer fears chilling effect after police seized posters
items.description: Police are assessing posters seized from a Canberra venue under new Commonwealth hate speech laws.

items.title: In her memoir, Gisèle Pelicot reveals the man she kept hidden
items.description: The world knows Gisèle Pelicot as the woman who waived anonymity during France's most infamous rape trial. But in her new memoir she reveals an unexpected story — the boyfriend she kept hidden and the love that helped her face an open courtroom.

items.title: Coles manager admits dog food price moves were outside 'guardrails'
items.description: A second Coles manager has been grilled in the federal court over whether rushing a product onto a "Down Down" promotion could have broken internal guidelines.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: Museum robberies, the Lunar New Year and a new shadow cabinet
items.description: It has been a huge week in news. Did you catch these stories?

items.title: Grieving dad plans surf lifesaving gala after shark attack tragedy
items.description: One year after his daughter was killed by a shark, a proud Queensland surf lifesaver says her legacy lives in the ocean.

items.title: Over-policing of children in care is 'manufacturing criminals', experts warn
items.description: Experts say over-policing and the South Australia's youth criminal justice system is helping turn children in residential care into criminals.

items.title: Federal, state police target 'black flights', drug imports in remote north
items.description: A joint police taskforce has been launched in Far North Queensland to target the importation of illicit drugs, forced labour and sexual servitude.

items.title: More 'hard and fast' rain likely for soaked parts of north Queensland
items.description: A risk for further heavy rainfall and thunderstorms is possible in northern parts of the state today and into the weekend.

items.title: Investigation finds cave diver died after being separated from buddies
items.description: Australia's peak cave diving body rules out malfunctioning equipment as a factor in the death of a man while diving in SA's Tank Cave.

items.title: 'There were no cowards': Bombing of Darwin commemorated 84 years on
items.description: Eighty-four years after Darwin was bombed in the single largest foreign attack ever mounted on Australian soil, hundreds of people have gathered to remember.

items.title: Voll's first big step in 'massive role' as Australia beats India in second T20
items.description: The retirement of Alyssa Healy leaves a big hole at the top of the order, but Georgia Voll looks capable of stepping in after a career-best outing in Canberra.
